items.title: Show HN: Stop applying to jobs using AI-generated resume
items.summary: When LLMs hands you a resume or pdf it carry markers of how it was made, including the source. You can't see them on the page but applicant tracking systems can read it. So recruiters are flagging such profiles and rejecting them entirely. I had tested this across 40+ AI models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, etc) to produce a resume and every single file carried a marker. To solve this problem. I had built a free tool to show what your file says and gives you a cleaned version: - Drop your resume and get a cleaned copy - Free, no account. What it doesn't do: it won't rewrite your resume or make AI-sounding wording more human. It only deals with what's hidden in the file. It's a simple tool, but it feels absolutely necessary now as more people are using AI for generating their entire res

items.title: Show HN: Musset, open-source Scrivener alternative with an AI that never writes
items.summary: I’m writing my first novel and could not find an app that fit my workflow: quiet like iA Writer, organized like Scrivener, and with AI so I can discuss my book while I write it. It allows me to feel less “alone” and have a sounding board while I write. - A book is a folder of plain Markdown files. Musset commits to a git repo, tracks versions and drafts without you having to know git. - Revisions are CriticMarkup inside the text. It manages docx revisions too, so your editor can edit a Word doc and you import their comments. - PDFs are typeset using Typst, embedded in the app, following each language’s typographic rules. - Spelling and grammar are checked using LanguageTool, also embedded. - Mac/Word, WordStar, vi and Emacs keyboard modes. The AI is optional and uses your Codex or Claude C
